topic.title: We root for the man who 'lost sight of right or wrong'
topic.claim: Drishyam endures because we secretly agree that family is a valid defence for nearly anything.
topic.behaviour: Viewers rewatch Drishyam and debate the confession scene. The man says his family is everything and he'd go to any extent, and many still side with him.
topic.mechanism: Family is the one moral authority we rarely question. 'I did it for them' feels like a reason, not a confession.
topic.group: millennials who grew up on Hindi thrillers
real_details: A viewer rewatched Drishyam 1 after many years
Questioned why Ajay Devgn's character confesses vaguely to Tabu's character and her husband
In the scene he calls himself a fourth-grade dropout
He says his family is most important and he'd go to any extent
He says he lost sight of right or wrong in that moment
The viewer worries it's risky if someone were recording
topic.why_now: Fresh rewatch debate shows the film still divides viewers a decade on.

score.reason: mirror, group, and arguable all land; fresh angle on a known film
score.best_hook: Drishyam's hero says 'I did it for my family.' Ten years later, we still refuse to call that a confession.
